title: Consolidate enterprise SDK signals for polyglot clients, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Collect, normalize, and prioritize outstanding enterprise requests about SDK language support, authentication/rotation patterns, and streaming ergonomics. Many large customers (regulated finance and healthcare pilots) have submitted similar asks independently; we need a single canonical decision path so engineering can scope a prioritized roadmap for the April SDK release without duplicative design work.
acceptance_criteria: Create a canonical signal document summarizing customer requests, severity, and representative use-cases
Agree on a prioritization rubric (security-sensitive, implementation complexity, adoption lift, telemetry) with Eng/Design/Support
Produce a minimal API/contract proposal for streaming ergonomics (reconnect semantics, backpressure, event IDs, resumability) reviewed by eng
Prototype client adapters for two new enterprise-focused languages (Go and Rust) with token-rotation and SSO patterns documented
Telemetry queries that surface retry/connect failures and per-language adoption added to the SDK dashboard
notes: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened after collating 12 customer threads from Support + three account exec summaries. Primary asks: (1) formal token rotation patterns, (2) SSO/SAML + delegated SSO examples, (3) streaming reconnect semantics and durable resume, (4) first-class Go/Rust examples for enterprise stacks.

2026-03-11: Quick sync with Eng lead (Maya Chen) and Design (Liam Ortiz). Eng flagged two blockers: API surface changes for resumable streams may require runtime SDK hooks (ENG-1842) and SSO examples require changes to onboarding docs + sample servers.

2026-03-12: Customer interviews scheduled (3 enterprise customers) to validate trade-offs between resumability vs. at-most-once semantics. Design to draft two UX options: 'auto-resume with idempotency tokens' vs 'stateless reconnect with server-side rehydration'.

2026-03-13: Decided to prototype Go + Rust client adapters (priority) and iterate on Python/JS ergonomics later. Security agreed token-rotation pattern must support short-lived tokens with client refresh hooks; include mTLS as an enterprise option for private deployments.
next_steps: Run three customer interviews (scheduled week of 2026-03-15) and capture acceptability criteria for streaming resumes
Eng to allocate 2 sprints to a minimal Go + Rust prototype (ENG owners: Ethan Morales, Priya Singh)
Design to produce a short contract doc for stream reconnect semantics by 2026-03-20
Create telemetry board cards to expose per-language connection and token-refresh failure rates
Schedule security review for token rotation/mTLS patterns during the week of 2026-03-22
